q: we carried out a large-scale survey aimed at how AI assistants are used, focusing on specific software development activities and stages. We collected opinions of 481 programmers
r: IC1: a developer survey on AI assistants' usage, not coding agents, SDD or context files.

q: This work serves as both a conceptual foundation for the emerging field of AI-augmented software engineering and a technical roadmap for advancing research and practice in coding agent systems.
r: IC1: a broad survey of vibe coding and code LLMs, not SDD, context mechanisms or an evaluation or comparison of coding agents.

q: we first construct an evolution-aware repository-level code generation dataset, namely HumanEvo, equipped with an automated execution-based evaluation tool
r: EC1: benchmark of function-level generation by LLMs given repository context, with no agentic behaviour.

q: These results show that coordination among AI coding agents can be measured directly
r: Include: controlled comparison of coding-agent team configurations with ten runs per cell and cost metrics; the contribution is the measurement method.

q: We audit 2,385 evaluation traces from 15 agent benchmarks
r: IC1: audits general agent benchmarks (web research, science, ML) for reward hacking, not software development agents specifically.

q: The dominant benchmark format focuses on short-horizon repair
r: EC6: a data factory mainly for bug-fix and issue-repair tasks (SWE-bench style).

q: we propose CodeTeam, an LLM-based multi-agent framework
r: EC5: a new multi-agent framework tested on existing benchmarks (SketchEval, NL2RepoBench), nothing new for the evaluation method.

q: This survey examines agentic artifact creation, which we define as stateful construction in which an AI system materially constructs or revises a deliverable
r: IC1: a survey of agentic creation of images, video, text and other artifacts, not coding agents.
